name: Executive order of March 24, 1883 fixing the boundaries of the Mescalero Apache Reservation
promises: The Indian Claims Commission found that this order defined the final boundaries of the reservation, adding two townships at the northwest corner including the Sierra Blanca, for a reservation of 474,240 acres, which became the Mescaleros' permanent home.
Royce maps the lands that earlier executive orders had included in the reservation and that were later relinquished (area 643).
today: The Commission held in 1966 that the United States took the Mescalero Apache Tribe's Indian title to its New Mexico lands without compensation on May 29, 1873, the date of the first reservation order, not on the date of this order. The claim (Docket 22-B) was settled by compromise in 1967 for a final judgment of $8,500,000.00.

openQuestions: Lands dropped from the reservation by this and earlier orders (Royce area 643) were part of the aboriginal claim the Commission dated to 1873; no finding ties a loss to this 1883 order, and an executive-order reduction alone is not a breach under the project rule.
The Mescalero Apache Tribe's own account of the 1883 boundaries was not located.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Mescalero, Mescalero 1883; United States v. Mescalero Apache Tribe, 207 Ct. Cl. 369 (1975) concerns interest on trust funds, not land; nothing new.
